## Setting Up the Conflict Structure

**Regular $k$-gons inside a regular $n$-gon.** A regular $k$-gon inscribed in a regular $n$-gon requires $k \mid n$, with vertices forming a coset of $\langle n/k \rangle$ in $\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$. Two vertices $i, j$ lie in the same $k$-gon iff $i \equiv j \pmod{n/k}$.

**Factoring 2002** $= 2 \times 7 \times 11 \times 13$. Divisors of 2002 less than 500 (and $\geq 3$): $7, 11, 13, 14, 22, 26, 77, 91, 143, 154, 182, 286$.

Setting $m = 2002/k$, the $m$-values are $\{286, 182, 154, 143, 91, 77, 26, 22, 14, 13, 11, 7\}$. Two vertices conflict iff $m \mid (j-i)$ for some $m$ in this set. Since every $m$ here is divisible by 7, 11, or 13, and 7, 11, 13 themselves appear, this simplifies to:

$$i \text{ and } j \text{ conflict} \iff 7 \mid (j-i) \text{ or } 11 \mid (j-i) \text{ or } 13 \mid (j-i).$$

**CRT decomposition.** Via $\mathbb{Z}/2002 \cong \mathbb{Z}/2 \times \mathbb{Z}/7 \times \mathbb{Z}/11 \times \mathbb{Z}/13$, two vertices conflict iff they share the mod-7, mod-11, **or** mod-13 coordinate. (The mod-2 coordinate causes no conflicts, since $k=1001$ and $k=2002$ are $\geq 500$.)

## Chromatic Number

**Maximum independent set.** An independent set requires all vertices to have distinct mod-7, mod-11, and mod-13 values. Since there are only 7 residues mod 7, the maximum independent set has size **7**.

**Clique lower bound.** Fixing mod-7 = 0 gives $2 \times 11 \times 13 = 286$ mutually conflicting vertices, a clique of size 286. So $\chi \geq 286$.

**Construction achieving 286.** Partition $\mathbb{Z}/7 \times \mathbb{Z}/11 \times \mathbb{Z}/13$ into 143 blocks indexed by $(s,t) \in \mathbb{Z}/11 \times \mathbb{Z}/13$:

$$\text{Block}(s,t) = \big\{\big(a,\; (s{+}a)\bmod 11,\; (t{+}a)\bmod 13\big) : a = 0,\ldots,6\big\}.$$

- **Distinct mod 7:** one cell per $a$. ✓
- **Distinct mod 11:** $(s+a) \bmod 11$ for $a=0,\ldots,6$ gives 7 distinct values. ✓
- **Distinct mod 13:** $(t+a) \bmod 13$ for $a=0,\ldots,6$ gives 7 distinct values. ✓
- **Coverage:** cell $(a,b,c)$ lies in block $((b{-}a)\bmod 11,\; (c{-}a)\bmod 13)$, uniquely. ✓

Each block yields 2 independent sets (mod-2 = 0 and mod-2 = 1), giving $143 \times 2 = 286$ independent sets of size 7 covering all 2002 vertices. So $\chi = 286$.

## Minimum Sum

With 286 colors, each class has exactly $2002/286 = 7$ vertices. Using colors $1, 2, \ldots, 286$:

$$\sum_{i=1}^{2002} a_i = 7 \times (1 + 2 + \cdots + 286) = 7 \times \frac{286 \times 287}{2} = 7 \times 41041 = 287287.$$

**Optimality:** Any proper coloring needs $\geq 286$ colors (since each class has $\leq 7$ vertices). With exactly 286 colors, all classes must have size 7, forcing the sum above. Using more than 286 colors only increases the sum (some class shrinks, requiring a higher color value). Hence this is optimal.

Final Answer: $\boxed{287287}$
